explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/6: with d_n = p_{n+1} − p_n, are there infinitely many n with d_n < d_{n+1} < d_{n+2}? The page records yes (Banks–Freiberg–Turnage-Butterbaugh). `primeGap n` is `Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n+1) − Nat.nth Nat.Prime n`; truncated subtraction is never active because primes increase. 0-indexing is immaterial. Faithful.
